note: The iOS privacy manifest's own part (PrivacyInfo.xcprivacy): no tracking, and the reason for each required-reason API the app's code reaches. The collected data types come from collection.json. Each SDK ships its own manifest as well; usedBy names the packages in this app that reach the API, and check.mjs fails when one is no longer a dependency or a reason code is not one Apple allows for that API.

accessedApis.why: React Native and Expo keep the app's own settings (language, update state, launch flags) in its own UserDefaults. Only this app reads them.
The offline cache, the image cache and the files the app writes are inside its own container; their timestamps decide what is fresh. No file outside the container is read.
React Native measures time between events in the app (timers, animations, the session heartbeat) from the system's uptime. It is never sent anywhere.
Before a download or the offline cache is written, the free space is checked so the write does not fail part way.
